The optional Resend command is an explicitly user-initiated test send to the user's own inboxes and defaults to dry-run. remediation.suggestion: Keep the dry-run default and require explicit confirmation before any live send. Validate that recipients are user-controlled test inboxes.

content.user_title: Build and QA responsive email HTML
content.value_statement: Email HTML often breaks across Outlook, Gmail, mobile clients, dark mode, and images-off conditions. This skill creates a table-based build and a clear QA record for those delivery risks.
actual_capabilities: Creates single-column, table-based email layouts with inline styles.
Checks light and dark mode colors for contrast and forced inversion risks.
Produces an estimated or measured client-render matrix for Gmail, Outlook, Apple Mail, iOS, and Android.
Specifies alt text, image-off fallbacks, solid background fallbacks, and bulletproof CTA buttons.
Checks that the plain-text version preserves the main message, CTA, and destination URL.
Routes copy changes and scoring work to the related skills instead of silently changing copy.
limitations: It does not write or revise email copy.
It does not send campaigns or replace a real inbox-preview test.
Client outcomes are estimates unless the user provides a seed-list or preview result.
It does not score email quality or calculate SEND metrics.

use_cases.title: Build a promotional email
use_cases.description: Turn approved campaign copy into responsive HTML with image-off and dark-mode safeguards.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Outlook rendering
use_cases.description: Review existing HTML for Outlook desktop limitations and document practical layout fixes.

use_cases.title: Prepare a newsletter handoff
use_cases.description: Create an accessibility checklist, client matrix, and plain-text parity review before QA handoff.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic email build
prompt_templates.prompt: Build responsive email HTML from this approved subject, body, CTA, and destination URL: [paste content]. Use the standard client set.

prompt_templates.title: QA existing email HTML
prompt_templates.prompt: QA this email HTML for Gmail, Outlook, Apple Mail, iOS, and Android. Report dark-mode, accessibility, and image-off issues: [paste HTML].

prompt_templates.title: Fix an Outlook issue
prompt_templates.prompt: This email breaks in Outlook desktop. Review this HTML, propose table and VML-safe changes, and label all results as Estimated until tested: [paste HTML].

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a complete render handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Build and QA this newsletter using the supplied creative, plain-text version, brand constraints, and target clients. Return HTML, an accessibility checklist, client matrix, image-off notes, and parity results: [paste materials].

output_examples.input: Build a product update email for Gmail and Outlook.
output: A responsive table-based HTML layout with inline styles.
A render matrix that labels Gmail and Outlook results as Estimated.
Image-off fallbacks, a bulletproof CTA, and plain-text parity notes.

output_examples.input: QA this existing email for dark mode and accessibility.
output: A pass or fail checklist for contrast, alt text, reading order, language, and font size.
Specific dark-mode risks and recommended HTML or CSS adjustments.
Open items requiring a real seed or inbox-preview test.

best_practices: Provide approved copy, a destination URL, and target clients before requesting a build.
Treat all untested client-render results as Estimated until a real preview or seed test confirms them.
Review the plain-text version with the HTML before handing the email to campaign QA.
anti_patterns: Do not place a CTA, price, or essential claim only inside an image.
Do not use flexbox, grid, or external stylesheets for layout-critical email content.
Do not claim a client passes without a measured test or documented support basis.

faq.question: Does this skill write email copy?
faq.answer: No. It builds and QA checks HTML from approved copy or existing HTML.

faq.question: Which email clients does it cover?
faq.answer: The standard set includes Gmail, Outlook desktop and web, Apple Mail, iOS Mail, and Android mail clients.

faq.question: Can it confirm live rendering?
faq.answer: Only when the user provides a real seed-list, inbox-preview, or render-preview result. Otherwise results are Estimated.

faq.question: Does it support dark mode?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks explicit colors, contrast, forced inversion risks, and logo visibility.

faq.question: Does it create a plain-text version?
faq.answer: It checks parity with a supplied version and can produce one when none is supplied.

faq.question: Can it send the email?
faq.answer: It documents an optional Resend test for the user's own inboxes. Live sending requires an explicit --live flag and user confirmation.
